reason: E1 shows W-rich precipitates in a different alloy system (TiZrWMo) and links uniform precipitates to high dynamic strength, but it does not provide evidence for improved strain hardening, uniform elongation, or delayed localization, nor does it address the HfZrTiTa0.53 base alloy. The key premises about hardening mechanisms and ductility improvements are thus largely unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: W addition to refractory HEA can form nanoscale W-rich precipitates in a BCC matrix
Uniformly dispersed nanoscale precipitates improve strain hardening via Orowan bowing and back-stress
Precipitate-induced microstructural refinement delays shear localization under high strain rates
These mechanisms lead to increased dynamic yield strength and improved uniform elongation
The cited Ti40Zr40W10Mo10 alloy behavior generalizes to the HfZrTiTa0.53 system
